children: Grave robbing might seem like the stuff of horror films, but back in the 18th century it was a remarkably common activity, and in one way actually contributed towards the evolution of medicine and surgery. It was only legal for surgeons to carry out anatomies on the bodies of convicted murderers who were hung for their crimes – but as these usually numbered only around 20 or 30 a year, this wasn’t enough to satisfy the need of the medical experts (who would perform autopsies to educate their students as well as learn more about the human body). Grave robbing brought body snatchers money, while surgeons could charge money to people who wanted to watch a dissection.

children: For Bloom to be standing next to an idle spade is significant.  In Judaism, it is customary for the community to bury the dead – to take up shovels themselves and cover the coffin.  It is the very definition of a “Mitzvah” – a final act of kindness that can never be returned.  At a Jewish funeral, this custom is ritualized; it’s highly unlikely that Bloom would not be aware of it.
“He stepped aside nimbly”.  Stepping away from the shovel in this context is symbolic.
